name: Data Lifecycle Placement
summary: Place each datum from explicit writer, reader, scope, freshness, retention and deletion requirements rather than prompt convenience.
context: An Agent combines transient context with Session, user, app or cross-session data.
Large payload, tenancy, freshness, retention or deletion requirements exist.
forces: Transient context is cheap to govern but must be supplied every invocation.
State is convenient but needs schema, conflict and freshness policy.
Artifacts add explicit I/O; memory adds ingestion, retrieval and deletion ownership.
decision: Use invocation context for small transient data, state for small mutable process facts, artifacts for large versioned payloads and memory for intentional cross-session recall.
Define writer, readers, scope, freshness, retention and deletion before selecting an ADK surface.
implementation: Validate scoped state keys before mutation and namespace independent writers.
Load versioned artifacts only when the model needs their content.
Make memory ingestion, identity filtering and deletion propagation explicit service policies.

observable_contract.statement: Invocation context is model-visible for one run and absent from Session state and history.
Session, user, app and temporary state have distinct materialization and persistence behavior.
Large payloads retain artifact version and scope and enter model context only after explicit load.
Cross-session recall requires explicit ingestion and identity-scoped search independent of source Session deletion.

failure_modes.statement: State remains stale or a large transient payload is resent on every invocation.
Prefixed user or app state bypasses Agent state_schema validation.
Deleting a Session is assumed to delete retained memory or user-scoped artifacts.
A memory adapter ignores app or user identity and returns another principal's data.

counterexamples.context: A pure local function receives all data as normal parameters and nothing crosses an invocation.
counterexamples.preferred: Use ordinary function parameters without an Agent data abstraction.

counterexamples.context: A current deterministic lookup belongs in a transactional system of record.
counterexamples.preferred: Use a database or API tool rather than long-term Agent memory.

adk_versions.notes: RunConfig context, state scopes, artifact versions and memory ingestion/search were exercised at the pinned commit.
The placement decision is portable, but concrete namespaces and deletion APIs require adapter-specific validation.

source_evidence.claim: RunConfig adds per-invocation model contents without writing Session history.
Session utilities separate app, user, session and temporary state deltas.
Artifact service defines versioned save, load, list and delete operations with distinct namespaces.
Memory requires explicit ingestion and app/user-scoped search but has no portable delete contract.

lab_evidence.claim: Transient context, state, artifact and memory variants produce the same scripted answer with different persistence.
Tests expose scope lifetimes and prefixed-key schema bypass.
Artifact scope, version, delete and explicit model visibility are verified.
Memory survives source Session deletion and remains separate from new Session state.
Tests expose stale state and repeated 20 KB transient context.
A deliberately broken adapter leaks Alice's memory to Bob.

rejected_decisions.decision: Store every datum in one Session state blob and inject it into every prompt.
rejected_decisions.reason: Scope, freshness, token cost, retention and deletion become implicit and coupled.
rejected_decisions.replacement: Select context, state, artifact or memory from an explicit lifecycle contract.
